notes: The word is a compound of 'mae' (mother) and 'nam' (water), highlighting the life-giving nature of rivers in the landscape.
Do not confuse this with 'nam' (water) or 'khlong' (canal/waterway). While 'nam' refers to the liquid itself, 'mae nam' specifically describes the large, flowing natural body of water.
